steps.body: To compare two lengths, put them side by side from ONE start line, then read the far ends: the one reaching farther is longer.
steps.narration: To compare two lengths, put them side by side from ONE start line, then read the far ends: the one reaching farther is longer.

widget.prompt: Measure the rope. Align zero with its start, then place 6 one-unit blocks with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: 6 equal blocks cover the rope exactly — same start, no gaps, no overlaps: that number IS its length.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Two ribbons from one start line; one reaches farther. The farther one is…
predict.reveal: Reach past a shared start line is exactly what LONGER means; weight never entered the test.

cml.actionGoal: Compare fairly — same start line, level seesaw, one sorting rule — for kmd compare length.
invariants: Fair comparison has fixed rules: lengths compare from one same start line, weights compare by which pan sinks, and sorted groups compare by their counts — the anchors for kmd compare length.
misconceptions: Judging length before aligning starts, reading size as weight, or comparing groups by how much space they fill instead of their counts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the starts were not lined up, could the far ends still settle which is longer?

widget.prompt: Compare the three ribbons from one start line and tap the longest.

items.label: top ribbon
items.feedback: The top one measures 6 cubes — shorter than 8. Count the unit ticks, not the look.

items.label: bottom ribbon
items.feedback: The bottom one measures 4 cubes — shorter than 8. Count the unit ticks, not the look.

widget.missFeedback: From one start line the far end decides: the longest reaches 8 cubes.
widget.successFeedback: Right — same start line, so the farther end IS the longest.

widget.prompt: Two runners race, but one starts ahead. Is the race a fair length test?

options.label: No — comparisons need one same start line
options.feedback: Correct — a head start fakes extra length; lining up the starts makes far ends comparable.

options.label: Yes — finishing first is all that counts
options.feedback: The head start stole distance; the finish alone cannot untangle it.

options.label: Yes, if they run fast
options.feedback: Speed cannot fix a crooked start — the compared distance is wrong.

options.label: Races cannot be compared
options.feedback: They compare fine once both start together — that is the whole fix.
